whyItMatters: Runtime overrides are powerful because they can change what a task executes under without changing the task definition itself. The key risk is the privilege delta introduced by the override.

threatContext.attackerBehavior: An attacker may override the task role at runtime to execute under a stronger identity than the service normally uses.
threatContext.realWorldUsage: This is a practical abuse path because runtime overrides can look like flexible orchestration while still activating materially different permissions.
threatContext.whyItMatters: The strongest signal is not that an override exists, but that it changes the effective role or increases available privilege.
threatContext.riskAndImpact: If missed, attackers can borrow the cover of an existing task family while swapping in a more powerful role only at execution time.

requiredLogSources: AWS CloudTrail management events for ECS
loggingRequirements: RunTask overrides must be preserved as structured data where possible.
The platform should know the default taskRoleArn and executionRoleArn for the task definition.
The detector should compare default and overridden roles semantically.
limitations: String searching for taskRoleArn in serialized JSON is unreliable.
Not every override changes privilege; some only alter commands or environment variables.
Some legitimate operations teams do use runtime overrides as part of approved workflows.

enrichment.description: Compare the default task role and the runtime role for permission, trust, and scope differences.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Finds meaningful privilege changes instead of noisy override presence.

enrichment.description: Distinguish role overrides from command, environment, or placement overrides.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Prevents every override from becoming a high-severity alert.

enrichment.description: Determine whether the actor and workflow are approved to override roles for this task family.
enrichment.falsePositiveReduction: Separates sanctioned exceptions from suspicious runtime role swaps.

logicExplanation.humanReadable: This rule should compare the task definition's default role with the final runtime role used by the task. The highest-value branch is when the runtime override changes the effective role and meaningfully increases task privilege or scope.
conditions: runtime override changes the final task role or privilege level compared with the default task definition
override is not part of an approved override workflow
logicExplanation.tuningGuidance: 1. Parse overrides structurally, not as plain text. 2. Compare default and runtime roles semantically. 3. Escalate only when the override changes privilege or authorization scope.
logicExplanation.whenToFire: Fire when RunTask uses a runtime override that materially changes the effective task role or increases workload privilege.

quality.falsePositiveRate: Low-Medium with override diff analysis; high when only checking for the literal taskRoleArn field

deployment.scheduling: Real-time is useful because overridden task roles can be used immediately.
considerations: This is the runtime-diff companion to `det-071`.
